items.title: ‘Honkai: Star Rail’ Version 4.7 “Now, Lay Laughter to All Stars” Lands 11 November
items.summary: Today, publisher HoYoverse announced that Version 4.7 for their ever-popular free-to-play fantasy sci-fi turn-based role-playing game title 'Honkai: Star
items.content:
Today, publisher HoYoverse announced that Version 4.7 for their ever-popular free-to-play fantasy sci-fi turn-based role-playing game title ‘Honkai: Star Rail’ will launch on 11 November. Dubbed “Now, Lay Laughter to All Stars”, players will assist in Planarcadia’s final performance to determine fate’s course. An animated short will also debut on the day of this patch’s launch. Aeon ★ Aha officially makes THEIR debut. Not only are THEY the director of this universe-wide performance, but THEY will also join the fray to initiate the final “Phantasmoon Games.” In this apocalyptic spectacle, THEY will battle the awakened leviathan, the Voracity, and stand alongside the Trailblazer in a showdown that will decide the destiny of the universe. Don’t look at me, that’s THEIR script. THEY also have codes for you to redeem in-game and over at HoYoLab within 23 hours of this article’s publication: “NEVERGONNAGIVE”, “NEVERGONNAMAKE”, “AHABLESSYOU”. …Wait a minute, these codes… Acheron, kindly smite me— Oh, and Silver Wolf LV.999, Sparxie, and Yao Guang will be getting their reruns while Acheron, Dan Heng • Imbibitor Lunae, and Jing Yuan will make their return in the second half of the patch.

For over a thousand Amber Eras, the leviathan, the Voracity, has been kept sealed by Aha’s “Phantasmoon Games.” But now, this behemoth is on the verge of a full awakening. To stop the leviathan from regaining its strength and devouring the entire universe, Aha has launched the hunt for the Voracity, summoning eight Supplicants to stage a spectacular performance known as the “Final Phantasmoon Games.”

Serving as the stage for this grand scheme, the Starfroster will set sail across the vast sea of stars. Tasked with the mission to lure the Voracity, this sweet, cake-like ship will bear witness to a grand finale spanning the cosmos, under the orchestration of The Laughter.

In this update, the limited 5-star character on the Path of Elation, Aeon ★ Aha, will officially make THEIR debut. As the creator of the “Phantasmoon Games,” THEY have spent millennia observing the joys and sorrows of the cosmos through theatrics and jests. This time, to stop the Voracity from devouring the universe, Aha has decided to take the stage THEMSELF, orchestrating the grand finale of hunting the Voracity.

In combat, Aeon ★ Aha will cause the Path of Elation to ascend for Elation characters, allowing each Elation character to unlock unique combat abilities. Furthermore, Aha will star as the leading role in the all-new “Aha Instant,” fast-forwarding the performances of Elation Skills. It is worth noting that the entire team will continuously accumulate Wishpower for Aha during battle. Once Wishpower is full, the Ultimate can be activated, dealing Elation DMG to all enemies. Not only that, but empowered by THEIR Aeonic Authority, ally attacks can directly reduce enemy Max HP.

In the first half of Version 4.7, the limited 5-star characters Silver Wolf LV.999, Sparxie, and Yao Guang will get their reruns, while Acheron, Dan Heng • Imbibitor Lunae, and Jing Yuan will make their return in the second half. Additionally, Version 4.7 will introduce a brand-new growth system, Affinitive Eidolon. Once Trailblazers own the designated characters and unlock their corresponding Affinitive Eidolons, they can unlock new additional abilities for these characters and their capabilities in combat. Acheron, Dan Heng • Imbibitor Lunae, and Jing Yuan will be the first to be enhanced by Affinitive Eidolons, unlocking exclusive combat buffs to provide indispensable help on the trailblazing expedition.

For the version events and gameplay, the all-new version event, “The Fluffy Movie: Overheated,” kicks off! Trailblazers can assist Aha in running a dessert shop to earn Gold Coins. The new combat event, “Interastral Peace Gala: Road to Fame,” will also be available simultaneously.

The permanent gameplay, “Currency Wars,” welcomes its massive second season, “Voyage Into the Canvas,” bringing a comprehensive update. Moreover, by participating in the “Phantasia Showstage” event, Trailblazers will have the chance to obtain Aeon ★ Aha’s limited outfit “Star Lotto” and other rewards! At the same time, the animated short “A Joyful Funeral Beneath the Moon” will be released on the day the version goes live.

Finally, upon the grand stage where mortals and gods perform as one, the stars will sing a brand-new track, “Ex Nihilo,” for Aha’s grand performance. This will deliver an immersive narrative experience for Trailblazers, uniquely crafted for the finale of the Planarcadia arc. Stay tuned!

Honkai: Star Rail is a free-to-play gacha title available on PC via HoYoPlay , PlayStation 5 consoles, and mobile devices ( iOS , Android via Google Play / Galaxy Store ), exceeding 150 million total downloads across all platforms since its launch back in 2023. Once again, Version 4.7 for Star Rail will drop 11 November.

Industry experts and players have chosen the best mobile games of 2026.

On October 28, Bangkok hosted the sixth annual GamingonPhone Awards ceremony, which honored the best mobile games as well as outstanding developers, publishers, and industry representatives. The winners were determined based on voting by a professional jury (50%), players (40%), and the GamingonPhone editorial staff (10%).

The top prize in the “Mobile Game of the Year” category went to Where Winds Meet, an open-world action RPG from EverStone Studio and NetEase Games. Meanwhile, the Players’ Choice award went to the life simulation game Heartopia, and the battle royale Free Fire was recognized as the Best Ongoing Mobile Game.

In 2023, the game won Apple's App Store iPhone Game of the Year, Google Play's Best Game, and BEST MOBILE GAME by The Game Awards. In 2024, it received the Golden Joystick Awards Still Playing Award (Mobile) and PlayStation® Partner Awards 2024 PARTNER AWARD among other honors. The game has been rated Teen by the ESRB and is also classified as PEGI 12. For more details and updates, please visit https://hsr.hoyoverse.com/ or follow @HonkaiStarRail on Twitter (X), Instagram, and Facebook. About Honkai: Star Rail Honkai: Star Rail is a space fantasy RPG title with a journey through immense worlds of the unknown. The player takes on the role of "Trailblazer," a courageous individual implanted with a powerful artifact, Stellaron, and bearing the determination to unravel the mysteries surrounding the fabled "Cancer of All Worlds" and Aeons. The game features fantasy elements with myths and legends integrated into the space sci-fi story. Combined with the intuitive turn-based combat system, diverse and distinctive companions, and immersive storylines that together compose an interstellar melody filled with captivating worlds, each brimming with unique cultures, awe-inspiring landscapes, and mythical wonders to explore. About HoYoverse HoYoverse is committed to providing immersive virtual world experiences to players around the world. We have brought fans popular games including Genshin Impact, Honkai: Star Rail, Honkai Impact 3rd, Tears of Themis, and Zenless Zone Zero, as well as a wide range of entertainment content. Community is at the heart of everything we do. We are devoted to engaging fans and fostering an enthusiastic and inclusive global community that provides access and encouragement for people to share their passion for ACG (Animation, Comics, and Games) through their own creativity and skills. Pushing the boundaries of imagination, we consistently explore cutting-edge game development technologies, and have accumulated leading technical capabilities in cel shading, cloud gaming, and other fields. In the future, we will continue to expand our content production, technology research, and publishing duties through operations in offices in Singapore, Montreal, Los Angeles, Tokyo, Seoul, and other areas. items.title: Astra Yao Will Still Play Support in Honkai: Star Rail
items.summary: Astra Yao of Zenless Zone Zero will be a 5-star Quantum Harmony character when she appears as a crossover unit in Honkai: Star Rail.
items.content:
HoYoVerse’s official social media accounts for Honkai: Star Rail released the key visual for how Astra Yao will look when she appears in the game. She will be a five-star Quantum Harmony character, and she’ll be part of the upcoming Zenless Zone Zero collaboration event.

The visual for Astra shows her lying on a CD while other records, music scores, and music-related paraphernalia surround her. This is an obvious reference to how she is a singer in her native game of Zenless Zone Zero . In her original game, she plays a more support-oriented role for the other Agents. Because of her Harmony Path, Astra will also be a support character in Honkai: Star Rail .

The Zenless Zone Zero collaboration will appear in Honkai: Star Rail Version 4.8. We already know that Ellen Joe will also show up as a playable character during this event. She will be a 5-star Ice Destruction character , meaning that she will play a DPS role. More information on their kits will appear later. The upcoming Special Program for Honkai: Star Rail will focus on Version 4.7, which will feature the playable version of Aha, the Aeon of Elation.

Honkai: Star Rail is readily available on the PS5, PC, and mobile devices. Ellen Joe and Astra Yao of Zenless Zone Zero will become playable characters in Version 4.8 .

items.title: Ellen Joe Is Still an Ice Character in Honkai: Star Rail
items.summary: There's a new teaser for Zenless Zone Zero's Ellen Joe ahead of her Honkai: Star Rail debut and it shows her element and path.
items.content:
HoYoVerse shared teaser art on social media for Ellen Joe from Zenless Zone Zero ahead of her debut as a playable character in Honkai: Star Rail . She will remain an ice element character there, just like she is in her original game. She is expected to show up in the game in the 4.8 update ,

Ellen Joe will be a five-star character when she launches in Honkai: Star Rail . All of her attacks will deal Ice damage. She will also be a Destruction unit. This means she’ll act as a DPS and her attacks should be able to do both single-target and AOE type attacks, with multi-target ones being the focus for her skills.

It’s possible we’ll learn a little more about the Honkai: Star Rail Zenless Zone Zero crossover and what Ellen Joe and Astra Yao will do when the characters appear soon. HoYoVerse announced a Special Program will air this week going over 4.7. That starts at 4:30am PT/7:30am ET on October 30, 2026 . The major character for that patch will be the five-star Aeon Aha . She’ll be playable following an appearance in the Planarcadia Trailblaze Mission storyline.

Honkai: Star Rail is available for the PS5, PC, and mobile devices, and Ellen Joe from Zenless Zone Zero will become a playable character in 4.8.

items.title: Honkai: Star Rail Version 4.6 "Dance With the Beast Before Moonrise" is Coming Soon
Why Honkai: Star Rail players talk quitting the game
items.summary: Honkai: Star Rail players and creators are debating whether to quit amid complaints about power creep, endgame design, events and story presentation.
items.content:
A wave of Reddit posts and YouTube videos about quitting Hoyoverse ‘s Honkai: Star Rail has put long-running complaints over power creep, endgame design and story presentation back at the centre of the game’s community debate.

The discussion does not establish that Star Rail is facing a measurable player exodus. The sources reviewed offer no player-count data. What they do show is a recurring concern from active and former players: the game can demand continued investment while giving some of them fewer reasons to log in.

YouTuber Pixel Tree , who said he had not played Star Rail for some time, argued that the current criticism was more notable because it was coming from the game’s own community rather than rival fandoms. He said seeing regular Star Rail creators express frustration suggested there was a genuine issue behind the wider social media debate.

Power creep is one of the complaints that appears most consistently across the Reddit post and creator videos. Players argue that the gap between older and newer characters has grown enough to change how they approach pulling, building and spending on units.

Read more: Hoyoverse announces Genshin Impact 7.1 Special Program date

GachaNekoVT , who said he still plays Star Rail, argued that the problem goes beyond new characters simply being stronger. Players may begin wondering how long a newly acquired character will remain useful before another unit performs the same role more effectively.

That can also make spending harder to justify. Building a character can take weeks or months, while obtaining higher Eidolons or signature Light Cones can require further investment. The concern is that the value of that investment may decline much faster than players expect.

Similar complaints in the material point to newer characters replacing older ones with comparable but stronger kits, widening the perceived gap between generations of units.

Endgame design has intensified that frustration. Players criticised rising enemy health and mechanics that favour particular character archetypes or team compositions. The Reddit author described the meta as increasingly punishing for players who want to continue using older characters.

Read more: Genshin Impact 7.0: Are Flins and Ineffa worth pulling?

Kekvin agreed that recent bosses and endgame modes can restrict viable teams, although he noted that power creep itself is hardly new to Star Rail. His criticism focused more on how newer encounters can turn difficulty into a question of which characters a player owns rather than how they use them.

The Reddit post from DependentNo1079 described Planarcadia as a story that was not necessarily bad but had failed to meet expectations. Its author pointed to repetitive animations, lengthy dialogue and presentation that can struggle to make major story moments feel distinct.

Pixel Tree discussed similar complaints, including repeated character poses, reused models and limited animation. The material also highlights the game’s frequent reliance on text screens during story sequences, an approach that has become a recurring joke within the community.

GachaNekoVT raised a different problem with the writing itself. He praised Star Rail’s characters and music but argued that recent stories can become difficult to follow because of the volume of lore, terminology and exposition.

items.title: Honkai: Nexus Anima Preview: HoYoverse’s Next Big Hit?
items.summary: Our Honkai: Nexus Anima preview explores HoYoverse’s colourful creature collector, covering auto-battles, team-building, and gacha mechanics.
items.content:
The gacha game landscape gets substantially busier every time HoYoverse announces a new title. Genshin Impact propelled the company into the stratosphere, while Honkai: Star Rail and Zenless Zone Zero have since catered to different tastes and helped the developer reach even more corners of the gaming world.

With that in mind, it isn’t surprising to see HoYoverse turn its attention to creature collecting with Honkai: Nexus Anima .

Honkai: Nexus Anima is a little bit of a lot of things. It combines HoYoverse’s familiar taste for dark, twisted storytelling with what might be the company’s most colourful world yet. Almost every corner bursts with detail, helped by the fact that this universe isn’t populated by people alone. It is also home to plenty of adorable monsters.

These creatures, known as Anima, have designs that wouldn’t look out of place in Pokémon. Instead of being divided into conventional elemental categories, however, they have more abstract, mood-driven attributes based on concepts such as Satiation and Dreams. It gives the game’s creatures a distinct identity, even if its inspirations are easy to spot.

You’ll use your Anima in auto-battles, with success largely depending on choosing creatures that work well together and placing them in effective positions. The characters you have access to provide special abilities, while fielding particular combinations of Anima can grant additional bonuses.

The battles themselves aren’t especially complicated, but there appears to be plenty of depth in building an effective team. You’ll want to spend time exploring and catching creatures, both to expand your tactical options and to make your existing Anima stronger.

That progression loop could prove compelling. There is something undeniably satisfying about watching the numbers rise, particularly when each improvement gives you another reason to experiment with your line-up.

The gacha system is split between pulling for characters, who provide new abilities, and pulling for Anima to obtain higher-rarity versions or upgrade those already in your collection. Anima can also be caught in the wild, which makes the monetisation side of the game a little unusual.

The full release will presumably encourage players to pull for the strongest creatures, but being able to find lower-rarity Anima and improve them through play is promising. It may give players the freedom to make their favourites viable by investing time rather than money.

Of course, this is still a gacha game, so monetisation will inevitably be part of the experience. Even if Honkai: Nexus Anima proves relatively welcoming to free-to-play players, it will still be designed to encourage spending.

I enjoy auto-battlers, but their hands-off nature can sometimes make them less engaging over time. Honkai: Nexus Anima’s progression systems should help keep players invested, although much will depend on the variety of challenges available beyond the main campaign.

HoYoverse has become increasingly good at creating entertaining side modes in its recent games, so there is every reason to expect more than a straightforward journey through the story. Whether those additional activities can keep the team-building interesting in the long term remains to be seen.

While I like most of what I’ve seen so far, the story feels a little flimsy. Once again, we play as a protagonist with no memory, a device that is starting to feel like a crutch in games of this kind. It makes delivering exposition easier, but there is something frustrating about beginning another adventure as a character who knows almost nothing about themselves or the world around them.

The villains are more encouraging. They bring a slightly more sinister edge to the otherwise colourful setting, and although the narrative currently feels a little crowded, there is real potential for this to become one of HoYoverse’s darkest stories yet. Given the territory explored by games such as Genshin Impact, that is no small claim.
